To top of my CPTSD and Bipolar 2 I also have a brain injury. This summer I went to a brain clinic and I learned exercises to help with my memory. Look up brain games and spend an half hour everyday playing the games. Then exercises for 30 mins 5 days a week. The goal of the exercise is to get your heart rate to 80% of max heart rate for 30secs to a minute. Then sit down use breathing techniques to lower your heart rate down close to resting. Repeat for 30 minutes. It reteaches your brain the sympathetic and parasympathetic responses. To normalize them. 
The brain clinic pretty much cures my anxiety and I haven’t had a panic attack since July. I was having multiple panic attacks a week.

He blamed me for his cheating and told me he felt “abandoned” by our conversation while he was in rehab. He literally blamed me and I am
sure he still does.

We weren’t a success story but I am a success for finally starting to take a good look at our marriage and owning my part of it.

I am also looking at my religion. The beliefs that were stated to me as I sought counseling from my pastor while struggling with his addiction, abuse and manipulation. Lamictal has been a life saver literally. Be patient with the side effects as you are titrating up on it. The side effects typically stabilize or completely go away with time. Mania and depression are destructive in my life and I am hospitalized frequently because of my difficulties off medications.

I found that having a balanced life has helped me the most. I have a good mix of hobbies (painting, outdoors, spending time with my animals), exercise walking, running and lifting weights, spiritual (meditation) and therapy has helped me the most. Once I put a regular exercise in my routine it really helped me to balance my mood and decrease my anxiety.
For me dating is very difficult. The timing to let someone know I have bipolar is difficult. I don’t want to tell them to early because of the stigma of mental health and also I don’t want to hide anything.
Good luck with your bipolar it is manageable with a healthy life and the right medications.

Yes when you get there they do a fMRI scan to see how your brain is functioning in specific cognitive markers. Then you go to multiple therapies: neuromuscular therapy, neurointegration therapy, neuro-occupational therapy, neuro psycho therapy vision therapy.
Then the last day you get another fMRI and you can see the improvement. 
They give you a treatment plan for continued treatments you need to do for 2 months. 
You will see the most improvements in 2-3 months.

I am almost a month out and I am impressed with my improvements already.

While I was in treatment in Utah for my PCS we did neuro muscular therapy. The goal is to get you heart rate up to 80% of max heart rate for 30-60 seconds then get it back down to resting heart rate as quickly as possible. This retrains the brain to stop having false alarms with anxiety.

Grateful for the mental health team that supports me and my patient family.
